title: AI Media Generation — Images, Audio & Video

sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

You'll understand the four categories of AI media generation (images, voice/audio, music, video), know the current best-in-class and free tools for each, learn how to write prompts that produce useful image output, and understand the specific failure modes that still limit each category. You'll generate your first AI image and explore at least one other category.

## The Media Generation Landscape (2026)

While text AI gets most attention, AI media generation has undergone its own revolution. Work that previously required professional software, production budgets, and specialist skills now produces usable outputs in seconds from a text description.

| Category | Free options | Best-in-class (paid) | Best use cases |
|----------|-------------|---------------------|----------------|
| **Image generation** | Bing Image Creator (DALL-E 3), Ideogram | Midjourney, Flux Pro, Recraft | Illustrations, concept art, social visuals, marketing |
| **Text-to-speech** | ElevenLabs free tier | ElevenLabs, PlayAI | Voiceovers, narration, accessibility |
| **Transcription** | Whisper (open source, free), FreeTranscriptions.com | Otter.ai, Descript | Meeting notes, lecture transcription, interview processing |
| **Music generation** | Suno free tier | Suno, Udio, Google Lyria | Background music, jingles, demo tracks |
| **Video generation** | Runway free tier | Sora 2, Kling 2, Runway Gen-4 | Short clips, concept visualisation, animation |

**The pace of change:** This is the fastest-moving area in AI. What is cutting-edge today becomes a free tier feature in 6-12 months. The skill to develop is not memorising specific tools — it's knowing what category to look for and how to evaluate new tools when they emerge. The underlying logic (text prompt → generated media) stays constant even as specific tools change.

## Image Generation — The Most Mature Category

AI image generation is the most developed and accessible media category. You describe an image in text and the model generates it. The quality gap between free and paid tools has narrowed significantly — free tools are genuinely good for many use cases.

**How the major tools differ:**

| Tool | Strengths | Weaknesses | Cost |
|------|-----------|-----------|------|
| DALL-E 3 (Bing Image Creator) | Accurate to prompts, good text in images | Style limited, less artistic | Free |
| Ideogram | Best-in-class text rendering in images | Slower than others | Free tier |
| Midjourney | Highest aesthetic quality, photorealism | Requires Discord, paid-only | $10-60/month |
| Flux Pro | Exceptional photorealism, good for people | Less stylised output | Paid per image |
| Recraft | Best for brand/UI/design consistency | Less suited for artistic images | Paid |
| Stable Diffusion | Fully local, completely free | Technical setup required | Free (local) |

**For most beginners:** Bing Image Creator is the right starting point. It's free, produces high-quality output, requires no account in Microsoft Edge, and handles most non-professional use cases well.

## Writing Image Prompts That Work

Image prompting is different from text prompting. The structure is more descriptive and visual, less instructional.

**The anatomy of an effective image prompt:**

```
[Subject] + [Action/Setting] + [Lighting/Atmosphere] + [Style/Medium] + [Technical details]
```

**Example — weak prompt:**
```
A coffee shop
```
→ Gets a generic, flat image with no character

**Example — strong prompt:**
```
A cozy independent coffee shop on a rainy day, warm amber interior lighting visible
through a fogged window, film photography style, shallow depth of field,
nostaligic mood, 35mm film grain
```
→ Gets a atmospheric, evocative image with the specific mood you wanted

**The most impactful elements to specify:**

**Subject and scene:**
- Be specific: "a Golden Retriever" not "a dog"
- Set the scene: "in a sun-drenched field of tall grass at late afternoon"
- Include action: "mid-jump, catching a frisbee"

**Lighting (huge impact on mood):**
- "golden hour light" — warm, long shadows
- "dramatic side lighting" — one strong directional source
- "soft diffused natural light" — even, gentle
- "neon-lit" — colourful, cyberpunk feel
- "candlelit" — warm, intimate, low light

**Style/medium:**
- "oil painting", "watercolor", "pencil sketch", "linocut print"
- "photorealistic", "digital art", "3D render", "flat design"
- "anime style", "Art Deco", "minimalist illustration"
- "film photography", "Polaroid", "35mm grain"

**Perspective/composition:**
- "bird's eye view", "worm's eye view", "wide establishing shot"
- "close-up portrait", "medium shot", "full body"
- "rule of thirds composition"

**What AI images still struggle with:**
- **Hands:** extra or missing fingers is still common — a known limitation across all tools
- **Readable text:** AI rarely renders legible words inside an image; use Ideogram if text matters
- **Exact faces:** depicting a specific real person accurately is unreliable (and often policy-restricted)
- **Complex scenes with many characters:** crowded scenes often have blending/proportion issues

## Text-to-Speech — Realistic AI Voice

**ElevenLabs** is the industry leader. You paste text, choose from hundreds of voices, and get natural-sounding speech — with proper intonation, natural pauses, and realistic breathing.

**Use cases that are production-ready today:**
- Voiceovers for YouTube videos without a recording setup
- Internal training videos with consistent narration
- Accessibility: audio versions of written content
- Podcast intros or transitions
- Demos and prototypes

**ElevenLabs free tier:** ~10,000 characters/month. Enough to narrate about 1,500 words — a short article or several shorter pieces.

**Voice cloning:** ElevenLabs and other tools can clone a voice from a short audio sample (about 1 minute). This creates legal and ethical obligations — cloning a voice without consent is problematic, and some jurisdictions are beginning to regulate it.

**Transcription (speech-to-text):**
The reverse capability — Whisper (OpenAI, free, open-source) transcribes audio with impressive accuracy across many languages. Practical workflow:
1. Record a meeting or lecture
2. Upload to a Whisper-powered service (many free web tools)
3. Paste the transcript into Claude → meeting summary + action items

This workflow replaces hours of manual note-taking.

## Music Generation and Video Generation

**Music Generation — Suno and Udio**

Suno generates complete music tracks — with instruments, structure, and optional vocals — from a text description. Free tier provides ~10 songs/day.

**Effective Suno prompts:**
```
Upbeat acoustic folk, 120 BPM, morning coffee mood, guitar and light percussion,
no lyrics, suitable for background music in a video
```

Or with lyrics:
```
An indie pop song about learning new skills, hopeful and energetic, female vocals,
electric guitar, verse-chorus-verse structure
```

**Realistic use cases today:** Background music for videos, podcast intros, demo tracks, jingle prototypes. Not a replacement for professional music production — but for everything that previously required either expensive licensing or compromising on quality, it's transformative.

**Video Generation — The Frontier (2026)**

Video generation has improved dramatically and is the category to watch most closely:

- **Sora 2** (OpenAI): Longer clips (up to 20 seconds), photorealistic, available in ChatGPT Pro
- **Kling 2** (Kuaishou): Strong motion consistency, good for realistic human movement
- **Runway Gen-4**: Best for artistic and stylised content; free tier available

**Current realistic capabilities:**
- Short clips (5-20 seconds) of atmospheric or abstract content
- Animating a still image (make a photo come to life subtly)
- Visual concept exploration before committing to real production
- B-roll footage for video projects

**Still developing:** Longer narrative video, consistent characters across clips, complex human action, accurate dialogue synchronisation. Video generation is improving faster than any other AI category — what's a demo today becomes a production feature within months.

**Ethical and legal considerations for media generation:**
- **Deepfakes and consent:** Using AI to create realistic images or video of real people without their consent is illegal in many jurisdictions and always ethically problematic
- **Voice cloning:** Cloning someone's voice without consent may violate laws around impersonation, fraud, and personality rights
- **Copyright in training data:** Most image generation models were trained on copyrighted images. The legal status of AI-generated output's copyright is still being litigated
- **Transparency:** When using AI-generated media professionally, consider disclosing that AI was involved — some platforms and publishers now require this

These aren't reasons to avoid media generation tools entirely — they're reasons to be thoughtful about how you use them.

sections.title: Media Generation First Contact
sections.content:
This workshop is about first contact — experiencing what each category feels like. You're not mastering any tool, just building an intuition for what's possible.

**Part 1 — Required: Generate Your First AI Image**

Go to [Bing Image Creator](https://bing.com/images/create) — free, no account needed in Edge.

First, try this structured prompt:
```
A friendly robot reading a book in a cosy library, warm amber evening light,
watercolor illustration style, soft and detailed, books on shelves in background
```

Look at the four generated variations. Examine them carefully:
- Which one is your favourite and why?
- Check the hands — how many fingers?
- What did the AI get wrong or strange?

Now try **your own prompt** based on the prompt structure from this lesson:
```
[Subject] + [Setting/action] + [lighting description] + [style/medium]
```

Try 2-3 variations, adjusting the prompt based on what you didn't like in the first result.

**Part 2 — Choose one more category to explore**

Pick one of these:

**Music — Suno:**
- Go to [suno.com](https://suno.com) (free account or no account needed to explore)
- Click Create, describe a genre + mood + tempo + whether you want vocals
- Listen to what it generates

**Transcription — Upload an audio clip:**
- Go to [freeconvert.com/audio-to-text](https://www.freeconvert.com/audio-to-text) or any free Whisper-powered tool
- Record yourself speaking for 1 minute (Voice Recorder app in Windows)
- Upload and transcribe. See how accurate it is.

**Voice — ElevenLabs:**
- Go to [elevenlabs.io](https://elevenlabs.io) and create a free account
- Click Text to Speech
- Paste 2-3 sentences of text, choose a voice, click Generate
- Listen. Does it sound human?

**Write down after your exploration:**
- Which category surprised you most with its quality?
- What would you actually use one of these tools for in your real work?
- What are the limitations that would prevent professional use right now?

sections.question: You need text to appear legibly inside an AI-generated image — for example, a social media post with a quote printed on it. Which tool should you prioritise for this specific requirement?
options: Midjourney — it produces the highest quality images overall
Bing Image Creator — it's free and widely available
Ideogram — it's specifically designed for accurate text rendering within images
Stable Diffusion — as an open-source tool it gives more control
sections.explanation: Text rendering inside AI images is a known weakness across most image generation tools — they frequently produce garbled, misspelled, or illegible text. Ideogram was specifically built to solve this problem and consistently outperforms other tools at rendering legible text within generated images. This is the one scenario where 'which tool generates generally better images' is less important than 'which tool handles this specific requirement.'

sections.content: **You've completed lesson 2-7.** You now have a complete map of the AI media generation landscape — image, voice, transcription, music, and video — with the practical knowledge of when free tools are sufficient, what current limitations to watch for, and how to write image prompts that get the result you want.
